body: chalk numbers run across the fire extinguisher and camera. the count skips one place, then resumes in a different hand.
title: Fire extinguisher beside the spare mark

body:
Diary line at the first trap: a torn pasture-test tag was caught beneath the spring. Its number belongs to a treatment drum the return ledger calls sealed.

The tag was sticky with the same blue coating as the trial seed.
title: First trap held a torn field tag

body:
Camp log: the pasture-study team slept here for three nights. On the fourth morning their cook poured out the water because it smelled medicinal.

My mother put it with the household bills so it would not be thrown away. It was the only part of the week that still had a date.

I do not know which of the two accounts was repeated afterward. The older one is the one I had in my hands that day.
title: Camp used by the pasture team

body:
Field diary: the first north arrow leads past drums used to wash pasture-test gear. One drum was already sealed and dripping pale rinse onto the grass.

The grass under the drip was dead to the root.
title: North arrow past the wash drums

body:
Photograph back: the second trap contained a torn soil-sample bag, not an animal. Blue granules beneath it matched the coating on the trial seed.

The granules had eaten a ring of bare ground around the bag.
title: Second trap held a sample bag

body:
Personal note from the field gate: green program badges signed the treatment sheet before anyone else. I copied one badge number after its wearer began shaking.

His hands were stained orange to the wrist.
title: Checkpoint checked field badges

body:
Road-crew receipt: barriers were moved downhill after a trial drum leaked. The billed hours match the day the pasture grass browned below the road.

The runoff left a yellow stain along the culvert.
title: Barriers moved after the spill

body:
Torn page: follow the upper north arrow to the trial gate and count every rinse can. The crew counted seven going in and six coming back.

They counted the containers before anyone counted who had carried them. I wrote the second number here while I could still remember it.

There may be a simple reason for the change. Nobody at the next stop could tell us what to do with the first version.
title: Upper arrow toward the trial gate
